newsitem.title: CANADA: Laidlaw sees US$550 mln Q2 gain on sale.
newsitem.headline: Laidlaw sees US$550 mln Q2 gain on sale.

text.p: Laidlaw Inc said it expects to book a onetime after-tax gain of US$550 million in its second quarter as a result of the sale of its solid waste management business to Allied Waste Industries Inc.
Laidlaw said the charge would equal US$1.75 per share for the quarter ended February 28, 1997 and will be listed as an unusual and non-recurring item.

Laidlaw said it will also take a US$133 million or US$0.42 cents a share writedown as an unusual and non-recurring item upon the completion of its purchase of 67 percent of Rollins Environmental Services Inc.
Laidlaw said it expects the Rollins purchase to be completed by late April or May.

A significant portion of the anticipated charge relates to the planned discontinuance of operations of the Laidlaw incineration facility at Clive, Utah, which is within 12 miles of a similar Rollins facility. The write down also will provide for the reconfiguration into a service center of the Laidlaw incinerator at Roebuck, South Carolina, and a rationalization of facilities in Nashville, Tennessee.
The combined landfill capacity of the merged entity will result in the abandonment of some expansion permits in Texas.

Synergies and cost savings from these changed circumstances within Laidlaw facilities and similar significant changes within Rollins' assets when the businesses are combined are now expected to produce annual improvements on the order of US$90 million, Laidlaw said.
